claim.markdown_says:
SignWriting:
1DA00-1DA36, 1DA3B-1DA6C, 1DA75, 1DA84, 1DA9B-1DA9F, 1DAA1-1DAAF Sinhala:   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 49431) ... then page-1221 opens with the bare line '0D81, 0DE6-0DEF' with no label
claim.why_it_matters: The 'Sinhala:' label from the top of PDF page 1191 is concatenated onto SignWriting's range line; Sinhala's ranges are orphaned at the head of the next page.

verdict.reasoning:
Independently confirmed on both sides, and every quote in the claim checks out verbatim.

PDF side (rendered at 300dpi): spec_p1220.png (printed folio 1190) ends its body with exactly two lines -- 'SignWriting:' followed by '1DA00-1DA36, 1DA3B-1DA6C, 1DA75, 1DA84, 1DA9B-1DA9F, 1DAA1-1DAAF' -- and then nothing but the '1190 (c)ISO/IEC 2023' footer and the license line. There is no 'Sinhala:' token anywhere on PDF page 1220; I read the printed glyphs directly. spec_p1221.png (folio 1191) opens its body with 'Sinhala:' on its own line, followed by '0D81, 0DE6-0DEF'.

Markdown side: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 49430 is 'SignWriting:' and line 49431 is '1DA00-1DA36, 1DA3B-1DA6C, 1DA75, 1DA84, 1DA9B-1DA9F, 1DAA1-1DAAF Sinhala:' -- the label welded onto the tail of the range line with a single space and no intervening newline. Line 49432 is blank, 49433-49435 are the page-1221 anchor/heading furniture, and line 49437 is the bare '0D81, 0DE6-0DEF' with no preceding label on that page.

I tested the standard rejection grounds and none of them apply:
- Not 'text actually present elsewhere in reflowed form': the issue is not a missing token but a token relocated ACROSS a page boundary and merged into a different logical line. Both halves of the Sinhala entry now sit on opposite sides of the page break, inverted relative to the PDF.
- Not page-break furniture: 'Sinhala:' is normative body content (a script name in the character-repertoire list), not a running header, folio, or license footer. The transcription's own furniture (the <a id="page-1221"> anchor, '## Page 1221', '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)') is correctly placed; the defect is separate from it.
- Not line wrapping or hyphenation: no wrap occurred. The PDF's range line fits and terminates at '1DAAF'; the added ' Sinhala:' is text the PDF line does not contain.
- It does change meaning at the line and page level. In this list the newline is semantically load-bearing: it is the sole delimiter between entry N's range data and entry N+1's label. Losing it makes 'Sinhala:' read as a trailing member of SignWriting's range list (it is not a code-point range at all), and leaves page 1221's opening range line unlabeled. Any per-line or per-page extraction -- 'what are SignWriting's ranges', 'what are Sinhala's ranges', 'what does page 1190 contain' -- returns a wrong answer against the markdown while returning a right one against the PDF.

The one point in the transcription's favor, which I weighed and found insufficient: read as one continuous stream with the page furniture stripped, the sequence is still '...1DAAF Sinhala:' / '0D81, 0DE6-0DEF' / 'Sogdian:', so a human reader tracking the alternating label/data rhythm could still recover the correct script-to-range mapping, and no code point is lost. That is why this is correctly graded structural rather than a semantic data loss -- but it is a genuine fidelity defect, not a formatting nicety.
verdict.corrected_description:
CONFIRMED as described, with one addition the claim omits: this is not a one-off but a systematic page-boundary artifact affecting the whole script-ranges list, and page 1220 is damaged at BOTH ends by it.

At the page-1219/1220 boundary the identical defect occurs: PDF page 1220 opens with 'Old_Turkic:' on its own line above '10C00-10C48', but markdown line 49374 reads 'Old_Turkic:' welded onto page 1219's last data line ('10A60-10A7C Old_Turkic:'), and markdown page 1220 therefore opens at line 49380 with the bare, unlabeled '10C00-10C48'. So markdown page 1220 both loses the label that belongs at its head and steals the label that belongs at the head of page 1221.

The general rule of the defect: wherever a script label falls at the top of a PDF page in this list, the transcription pulls it back one page and appends it, space-separated, to the final range line of the preceding page, destroying the newline that separates the two entries. Remediation should move 'Sinhala:' from the end of line 49431 onto its own line at the head of the page-1221 body (immediately before line 49437 '0D81, 0DE6-0DEF'), and should sweep the surrounding pages of this list for the same pattern rather than patching page 1220 alone.
